title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
purpose: Help the user understand an important empirical paper about measuring and forecasting agent capabilities without reading the full paper.

output.audience: An informed non-specialist reader following current developments
output.format: Well-structured prose with descriptive headings and optional sparing bullet points

strengths: NeurIPS 2025 Main Conference paper with direct relevance to agentic software work
Different evidence shape from TheAgentCompany: human baselines, statistical modeling, robustness checks and forecasting
Requires careful separation of observed results, qualitative interpretation and conditional extrapolation
Contains quantitative results whose meaning depends on success probability, task distribution and reference humans
limitations: English-to-German output combines comprehension, translation and summarization
Only the ten-page main paper is included; appendices remain outside the executable input
The main paper itself uses both 169 and 170 for closely related task counts and both 11 and 12 for frontier-model counts
The reported model results and forecasts belong to the frozen 2025 publication
